title: Payment processors can turn business exit fees into a measurable remedy while practical replaceability remains open
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission First American Payment Systems enforcement and refund-administration record; eligible small businesses are a remedy-program population, not a representative firm sample
geography: United States federal consumer-protection enforcement involving small businesses enrolled with First American Payment Systems

observations.period: June 2017–April 2020 alleged enrollment/fees; February 2025 refund distribution; January 2026 claims review

denominator.unit: businesses sent checks by the FTC refund program

alleged_fee_practice.value: hidden or unauthorized fees, including early-termination fees and zombie charges

claim_status.value: FTC currently reviewing claims; refund amount depends partly on how many businesses file

cash_receipt_and_business_exit.value: not observed in the public refund page

observations.method: Official FTC refund-program page checked September 17, 2026; retain checks sent, aggregate distribution, settlement amount, and claims-review status as separate administrator-reported measures, not as cashed-payment or business-recovery rates.
observations.uncertainty: The page does not publish individual amounts, check-cashing rate, failed-delivery count, claim denominator, fee incidence by business, switching costs, alternative processor access, revenue effects, or later business survival and exit.
observations.subgroup: Businesses enrolled with First American Payment Systems during the stated period and charged an early-termination fee; claimants, check recipients, nonclaimants, and businesses with prior credits are distinct groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: A refund can offset an unauthorized fee without restoring lost transaction capacity, time, or customer relationships; a processor’s exit fee may be costly precisely when a business has few practical alternatives.

related_sources.claim: FTC lists First American Payment Systems Settlement as an active January 2026 refund program.

boundary: This record establishes reported payment-processor fee allegations, recipient-counted checks, aggregate distribution, and claims-review status. It does not establish individual cashing, full restitution, processor switching, business survival, trust, collective action, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: FTC First American Payment Systems refund HTML retrieved without retaining a repository copy
